name: same-owner in-place MAC rewrite and forward
kind: constructive ordinary control derived from the selected workflow/API; specified, not implemented or timed
preconditions: RX packet is a valid writable direct mbuf, sole owner/refcnt=1
same configured port and TX offload constraints as selected source
no additional consumer requires original header/payload or physical duplicate
no added trust isolation or forced clone requirement
steps: receive original mbuf p from the same RX queue
enqueue p itself into the same rx_to_tx ring without dst allocation, data copy or source free
on ring rejection free p and account the same drop boundary
TX dequeues p, applies the existing update_mac_addrs semantics to the first 12 header bytes
submit p to the same TX queue; retain accepted mbufs under PMD ownership, free/account unsent mbufs
drain TX and release only after actual completion; retain faults/drops as explicit outcomes
output_equivalence: same packet length, same rewritten source/destination MAC, unchanged bytes after first 12, same per-queue ordering and legitimate drop rules; actual timing/drop rates may differ and are unmeasured
ownership: no early free of forwarded RX buffer; TX completion still required. RX descriptor replenishment is source-supported; source and copied destination use same pool
resource_comparison: ordinary path holds one mbuf across transfer, copy path holds source and destination during copy then destination until TX; no guaranteed numeric throughput result inferred
copy_benchmark_caveat: not equivalent to a benchmark whose declared purpose is to execute/measure copy operations; this is precisely why that benchmark alone does not establish application necessity for the copy
fallback: retain SW/DMA copy for a real documented shared/immutable buffer, mandatory clone, ownership or allocation constraint; none established for selected sample forwarding contract
decision: concrete ordinary elimination exists for useful forwarding under source-supported ownership; mandatory separate DMA-copy demand not established
not_claimed: all DPDK applications can omit copies
